summary: Jonathan Duquette is a scholar of Indology and philosophy who earned his PhD from Université de Montréal in 2011. He held fellowships at the University of Oxford (2015–2019) and research or lecturing posts at Cambridge (2019) and Birmingham (2020–2021).

Jonathan Edelmann specializes in Indology, religious studies, and philosophy. He completed his DPhil at the University of Oxford in 2009 and served as an assistant professor at the University of Florida in 2015.

Jonathan Geen is an Indology and religious studies scholar who completed his doctorate under Phyllis Granoff at McMaster University in 2001. He has taught at McMaster University, Butler University, and the University of Rochester.

Philosopher Jonathan Glover studied at Corpus Christi College, Oxford. He served as a fellow and tutor at New College (~1967–1998) and held posts at King's College London (~1998–2014), the Hastings Center, and the University of Oxford.

Philosopher Jonathan Lear studied at Yale, Cambridge, and Rockefeller University (PhD 1978). He taught at Yale (1978–1996) and Cambridge (1979–1985), and served as a distinguished service professor at the University of Chicago (2014–2022).

Jonathan Mark Kenoyer works in archaeology and Indology. He studied at UC Berkeley under George F. Dales (~1974–1983) and became a professor of anthropology at the University of Wisconsin-Madison around 1985.

Jonathan Scott was an Indologist and Iranian/Central Asian studies scholar who founded The Asiatic Society. He served as Professor of Oriental Languages at the Royal Military College, Sandhurst (1802) and the East India Company College (~1806–1809).

Religious studies scholar Jonathan Z. Smith studied at Haverford and Yale. He taught at Dartmouth and UC Santa Barbara before serving as Dean of the College at the University of Chicago (1977–1982) and president of the Society of Biblical Literature (2008).
Jong-Nam Choi is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who studied at Shitennoji University and completed a PhD at the University of Hamburg in 1998 under Lambert Schmithausen.

Jongcheol Lee specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology, earning a PhD from the University of Tokyo under Yasunori Ejima in 1994. He was a researcher at the University of Mysore (1992) and an associate professor at the Academy of Korean Studies.

Jongmyung Kim is a scholar of Buddhist studies, history, and religion who studied at Yonsei, Seoul National, and UCLA (under Robert E. Buswell Jr.). He served as an associate professor of Korean Buddhism at the Academy of Korean Studies.

Joryu Chiba was a scholar of Buddhist studies, history, and Japanology who studied and held multiple academic posts at Ryukoku University from 1950 to 1989. He also served as director of the Honganji Historical Materials Research Institute.

Jos Gommans is a historian and Indologist who studied at Radboud University and Leiden University, completing his doctorate under Jan C. Heesterman and André Wink. He joined the faculty of Leiden University in 1993, becoming a professor in 2011.

Linguist Jos. Schrijnen earned his PhD at KU Leuven in 1891 and studied at the University of Paris. He held professorships at Utrecht University (1912–1921) and served as professor and rector at Radboud University Nijmegen (1923–1938).

Linguist and Indologist Josef Baudiš studied at Charles University under Josef Zubatý and at Heidelberg. He served as a Privatdozent at Charles University (~1912–1914) and became a professor at Comenius University in 1924.

Indologist Josef Friedrich Kohl studied at the German University in Prague and earned his PhD at the University of Bonn under Willibald Kirfel. He was a Privatdozent at Prague (1943–1945) and an extraordinary professor at the University of Würzburg (1957).

Josef Horovitz was a scholar of religion and history who earned his PhD at the University of Berlin under Eduard Sachau. He served as Professor of Arabic at Aligarh Muslim University (1907–1914) and later as professor at Goethe University Frankfurt.
Linguist Josef Jungmann studied at Charles University in 1795 and later held a post there from circa 1815 to 1842.

Josef Kohler, who worked in Indology and history, studied at Heidelberg and Freiburg. He was appointed professor at the University of Würzburg in 1878 and professor of law and legal philosophy at Humboldt University of Berlin in 1888.

Ethnomusicologist and Indologist Josef Kuckertz completed his PhD and habilitation at the University of Cologne. He served as professor of musicology at the University of Cologne (1970) and as professor at the Free University of Berlin from 1980.
